Hi Rachel / David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are NorthGrove's consolidated redlines for the MSA and the Order Form annex focused on the on‑prem/VPC deployment (file: NGH_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx). Key items we flagged up front so you have context:

- License scope: clarify that runtime residency and snapshot delivery are limited to approved environments and to a single production datacenter per territory.
- Operator access / witness: request a witnessed snapshot handover and a 2‑week audit window where NorthGrove auditors can validate the snapshot.
- Escrow‑lite: propose an escrow‑like mechanism for encrypted snapshots and a proof‑of‑restoration exercise annually.
- KMS / key custody: we need either customer‑managed keys (bring your own KMS) or a documented handback procedure with attestation.
- Evidence retention: 7 years for forensic artifacts tied to PHI processing.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on the above and whether you anticipate any commercial impacts? We are aiming to get legal signoff and an order form executed by the end of February; if there are significant redlines that require executive approval it would change our timeline.

If it's helpful, procurement is happy to meet for a 30‑minute redlines walkthrough tomorrow afternoon (1/16) or Thursday (1/18).

Attachments: NGH_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx, NGH_OrderForm_Annex_SOW.pdf

Best,

>

I've done a first pass with engineering and our legal partner — high level: we can accept the tightened license residency language with a small clarification on permitted failover topology. Operator access and the witnessed snapshot request are the biggest items that will need a short legal negotiation and an ops procedure.

What we expect to be able to offer without further executive signoff:
- Customer‑managed KMS option (BYOK) for the encryption key used for snapshots.
- A runbook for witnessed snapshot creation and transfer; Redwood will provide a timeboxed window for a forensic observer.
- A defined audit window (we suggest 48 hours for active console access for auditors; longer access requires a validated business justification and an approved SOP).

Items that will likely require a legal compromise or commercial concession:
- Annual proof‑of‑restoration exercises tied to an escrow mechanism — need to agree scope and acceptance criteria.
- Retention clock for artifacts that contain PHI — need to confirm exact artifacts and whether Redwood is the retention steward or if NorthGrove will pull and store evidence.

I'm copying David (legal) and Michael (enterprise solutions) to align on redline language and any potential changes to the order form pricing. Would 1/18 at 10:00 PT work for a 30‑minute redline triage?

I attached a marked‑up order form annex with minor clarifications (NGH_OrderForm_Annex_SOW.pdf). Please let us know which items are negotiable vs. firm requirements.

Subject: Re: NorthGrove MSA + Order Form — on‑prem annex redlines (internal legal notes)

Rachel / Michael — internal legal read after Elena's packet. Attaching our suggestion doc (RGD_Legal_Suggestions.docx). Highlights: 

- Escrow‑lite: propose language that limits Redwood's obligation to produce encrypted runtime images + metadata and to provide cryptographic proof & key escrow instructions, but not to act as a perpetual custodian of unencrypted snapshots. This preserves liability boundaries while meeting the customer's need for recoverability.

- Witnessing / audit scope: suggest we offer a witnessed snapshot‑creation session + a secure transfer of a read‑only forensic bundle. The customer's request for a two‑week full access window looks excessive; recommend a scoped validation period (e.g., 72 hours) with an option to extend by mutual agreement and with a notarized request for escalated access.

- KMS: accept BYOK + documented handback. Add a clause for emergency key recovery that requires judicial process or a pre‑defined escalation channel — we cannot unilaterally hand keys without controls.

- PHI retention: seek to shift primary retention responsibility to customer where possible; Redwood can retain minimal forensic logs for 18 months by default and extend by contract for an agreed fee.

Next steps: I can convert the above bullets into redline text for the MSA and the annex. If we're comfortable with the 72‑hour witness window + BYOK + escrow‑lite language, I think we can avoid escalating to execs.

David Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance

Elena — following our internal review we've consolidated Redwood's position and attached a redline set that maps to NorthGrove's asks.

On Tue, Jan 16, 2028 at 8:15 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rachel / Michael — internal legal read after Elena's packet. Attaching our suggestion doc (RGD_Legal_Suggestions.docx). Highlights:...

Summary of Redwood positions (high level):
- License residency: we will accept the restricted residency language but will add permitted failover language limited to the named datacenter footprint.
- KMS: we can offer BYOK (customer‑managed keys) and will include an emergency key recovery process that requires escalation and documented approvals.
- Snapshot & witness: we propose a witnessed snapshot handover with a 72‑hour validation window for NorthGrove auditors (extendable by mutual written agreement). During the window Redwood will provide a read‑only forensic bundle; console access beyond that window will be treated as a separate engagement.
- Escrow‑lite & proof of restoration: Redwood will agree to an escrow‑lite deposition of encrypted snapshots and to run an annual proof‑of‑restoration exercise subject to mutually agreed success criteria and a modest fee for rehearsal.
- Retention: Redwood proposes baseline forensic artifact retention of 18 months; extended retention can be contracted for an additional fee.

Next actions:
1) Please review the attached redlined MSA/annex (NGH_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) and our annotated Order Form Annex (NGH_OrderForm_Annex_SOW.pdf).
2) If acceptable, sign the Order Form Annex via DocuSign (link: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/NGH-OrderForm-041).
3) If you prefer, we can run a 30‑minute legal/ops sync on 1/24 or 1/31 to finalize language and the runbook — please confirm preferred slot.

If any of the proposed compromises (72‑hour validation window, BYOK, escrow‑lite with rehearsal fee) are blockers for NorthGrove we'll escalate to execs for resolution, but David and I believe these strike a practical balance between auditability and operational safety.

Attachments: NGH_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx, NGH_OrderForm_Annex_SOW.pdf
